title: A novel indicator-based visualisation method to investigate diffusion behaviour of dissolved CO2 in hydrogels
author: Fladung, Langwald, et al.

steps.title: Prepare sodium silicate sol
steps.instruction: Combine 9 mL distilled water, 1 mL sodium trisilicate solution (Na₂O₇Si₃, 26.5 % SiO₂) and 3.2 g protonated Amberlite IR‑120 ion‑exchange resin; stir at 500 rpm for 15 min to obtain a 10 % v/v sodium silicate sol. Remove the resin by filtration, then distribute the sol into 1.5 mL aliquots in 2 mL reaction tubes. To each aliquot add 75 µL of 0.1 % aqueous bromothymol blue indicator and 300 µL f/2 marine microalgae cultivation medium.

substeps.instruction: Stir mixture at 500 rpm for 15 min.
Filter to remove ion‑exchange resin.
Aliquot 1.5 mL into 2 mL tubes.
Add 75 µL 0.1 % BTB indicator.
Add 300 µL f/2 medium.

steps.title: Initiate silica sol gelation
steps.instruction: For each aliquot, add 18 µL of 2 M tris(hydroxymethyl)‑aminomethane (TRIS) and mix thoroughly; the solution will turn from yellow to blue, reaching pH 8.0. Before gelation completes, transfer 150 µL of the blue‑activated sol into each of ten glass reaction vials.

substeps.instruction: Add 18 µL 2 M TRIS to each aliquot.
Mix thoroughly until colour changes to blue (pH 8.0).
Transfer 150 µL of the activated sol into each glass vial before gelation finishes.

steps.title: Prepare polymer hydrogels (agar etc.)
steps.instruction: Heat 1.818 mL of the chosen polymer solution (agar, agarose, carrageenan or gelatin). Add 75 µL of 0.1 % aqueous bromothymol blue indicator, then adjust the pH to 8.0 with 0.1 M NaOH or HCl. Dispense 150 µL of the hot mixture into each reaction vial. Allow to harden for 5–10 min at room temperature, except gelatin, which is hardened at 5 °C overnight.

substeps.instruction: Heat 1.818 mL polymer solution.
Add 75 µL 0.1 % BTB indicator.
Adjust pH to 8.0 using 0.1 M NaOH or HCl.
Fill 150 µL into each vial.
Harden: 5–10 min at RT (agar, agarose, carrageenan); gelatin at 5 °C overnight.

steps.title: Prepare calcium alginate cylinders
steps.instruction: Gel a large volume of sodium alginate solution in a beaker containing 2 % dye‑doped CaCl₂ cross‑linking solution for 48 h to form a hydrogel sphere. After complete gelation, cut cylinders of 6 mm diameter with a cutting tool. Insert each cylinder into a reaction vial using a thin syringe tip to allow air to escape; after removal of the tip the slightly oversized cylinder will fill any gap between gel and vial wall.

substeps.instruction: Gel sodium alginate in 2 % dye‑doped CaCl₂ for 48 h.
Cut 6 mm diameter cylinders from the gel sphere.
Insert a thin syringe tip into the vial.
Slide the cylinder into the vial, allowing air to escape.
Remove the syringe tip; the cylinder should snugly fit the vial.

steps.title: Store or ready samples for analysis
steps.instruction: Store all hydrogel‑containing vials in airtight screw‑cap bottles at room temperature, or proceed directly to measurement. Prior to CO₂ dissolution analysis, add 200 µL MilliQ water to each sample vial.

substeps.instruction: Store vials airtight at room temperature, or analyze immediately.
Add 200 µL MilliQ water to each vial before CO₂ analysis.
